analysis: Antithrombin III deficiency is primarily associated with an increased risk of thrombosis rather than hemorrhage, as it leads to a hypercoagulable state. Liver disease can also result in decreased production of clotting factors, contributing to hemorrhage. Thrombocytopenia, characterized by a low platelet count, directly increases the risk of bleeding.
